content.text: The pack flags its own coverage as incomplete, so I'll check the callers of the entry points directly.

`CircuitStateController.EnsureNotDisposed` is private. It is called directly from seven methods of `CircuitStateController`, and one strategy method reaches it indirectly. The devkb pack found nine functions in all, but I count eight. The ninth looks like the same set counted differently. The pack's coverage note says it is incomplete, so I grepped `src` for calls to those seven methods to check.

**Production methods that reach it**

Direct callers, each of which calls `EnsureNotDisposed()`:
- `CircuitStateController.CircuitState` (line 53)
- `CircuitStateController.LastException` (line 66)
- `CircuitStateController.LastHandledOutcome` (line 79)
- `CircuitStateController.IsolateCircuitAsync` (line 90)
- `CircuitStateController.CloseCircuitAsync` (line 110)
- `CircuitStateController.OnActionPreExecuteAsync` (line 126)
- `CircuitStateController.OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync` (line 196)
- `CircuitStateController.OnHandledOutcomeAsync` (line 222)

Indirect caller, one hop out:
- `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore` calls `OnActionPreExecuteAsync` (line 32), `OnHandledOutcomeAsync` (line 52) and `OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync` (line 56).

The `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy` constructor (lines 18–21) passes `CircuitState`, `IsolateCircuitAsync` and `CloseCircuitAsync` as delegates to `stateProvider.Initialize`. It doesn't call them itself, but anyone who uses the provider's state, isolate or close members reaches `EnsureNotDisposed` through them. Those provider members are public API; I did not trace them further.

The legacy `Polly` package (`CircuitBreakerPolicy`, `AsyncCircuitBreakerPolicy`) calls `BreakerController.CircuitState` and `.LastException`. I did not check which controller type `BreakerController` is. It is probably a separate legacy controller rather than this class, so I left those policies out of the list.

Beyond `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore`, I found no further production callers in `src`.

**Test files**

- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/Controller/CircuitStateControllerTests.cs`. This is the only one the graph lists. It has an `ObjectDisposedException` assertion on `IsolateCircuitAsync`, plus 34 more tests on the call paths.
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerResiliencePipelineBuilderTests.cs`. It mentions `ObjectDisposedException`, so it may check disposal behaviour. I did not open it, and the graph doesn't list it as a test of this method.

`test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/Controller/ScheduledTaskExecutorTests.cs` also mentions `ObjectDisposedException`. It tests a different class, so I excluded it.

Strategy-level tests of `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy` likely run these paths too. I didn't confirm that.
